title: Ideal-power torsion preserves injective modules over a Noetherian ring
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $K\subseteq A$ be an ideal, and let $E$ be an injective $A$-module [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Then the $K$-power torsion submodule $\Gamma_K(E)=\{x\in E\mid \exists n\in\mathbf N,\ K^n x=0\}$ [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor] is injective as an $A$-module. Here $K^n x=0$ means $a x=0$ for every $a\in K^n$; no finite-generation hypothesis on $E$ is imposed.

proof.text: Put $T=\Gamma_K(E)\subseteq E$, with its submodule structure from [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor]. By [lem-sf-baer-criterion], it suffices to extend every $A$-linear map $f:J\to T$, where $J\subseteq A$ is an arbitrary ideal, to an $A$-linear map $A\to T$. Fix such $J$ and $f$, and also write $f$ for its composite with $T\hookrightarrow E$. All modules are taken in a common universe containing $A$ and $E$.

source.place: Tag 0AVF, lemma-characterize-injective-bis, (1) iff (3); agent specialization to T.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], write $J=(j_1,\ldots,j_r)$. For each $i$, the definition of $T$ gives $m_i\geq0$ with $K^{m_i}f(j_i)=0$. Put $m=1+\sum_i m_i$; this also handles $r=0$. Since $K^m\subseteq K^{m_i}$, for $a\in K^m$ and $j=\sum_i b_i j_i$ we have $a f(j)=\sum_i b_i a f(j_i)=0$. Thus $K^m f(J)=0$.

source.place: Tag 08XW, lemma-injective-module-divide, (2); agent finite-generation argument using the stated torsion definition.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-artin-rees] with the finite $A$-module $M=A$, the submodule $N=J$, and the ideal $I=K$. The module $A$ is generated by $1$, and $A$ is Noetherian by hypothesis, so all its hypotheses hold. It gives $c\geq0$ such that $K^{m+c}\cap J\subseteq K^m J$. Set $n=m+c$. The map $f$ vanishes on $K^m J$: on an element $\sum_

u\in K^m$, $u_

u)=0$ by Step 2. Consequently $f$ vanishes on $J\cap K^n$.

source.place: Tag 00IN, lemma-Artin-Rees, applied to J contained in A; agent application.

proof.text: Define $h:J+K^n\to E$ by $h(j+k)=f(j)$ for $j\in J$ and $k\in K^n$. If $j+k=j^{\prime}+k^{\prime}$, then $j-j^{\prime}=k^{\prime}-k\in J\cap K^n$, so Step 3 gives $f(j)=f(j^{\prime})$; hence $h$ is well-defined. The formulas $h((j+k)+(u+v))=f(j)+f(u)$ and $h(a(j+k))=a f(j)$ show additivity and $A$-linearity. Its restriction to $J$ is $f$, and it is zero on $K^n$.

source.place: Tag 08XW, lemma-injective-module-divide, (2); agent construction of the extension on the sum ideal.

proof.text: Since $E$ is injective, [lem-sf-baer-criterion] applied to the ideal $J+K^n$ extends $h$ to an $A$-linear map $g:A\to E$. Put $e=g(1)$. For every $a\in K^n$, $a e=g(a)=h(a)=0$, so $e\in T$ by [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor]. For every $b\in A$, $g(b)=b e$ and $K^n(b e)=0$ by commutativity. Thus $\widetilde f:A\to T$, $b\mapsto b e$, is $A$-linear and extends $f$, because $g|_J=h|_J=f$.

source.place: Tag 0AVF, lemma-characterize-injective-bis, (1) implies (3); agent torsion-valued extension argument.

proof.text: The construction applies to every ideal $J$ and every $f:J\to T$. The reverse implication of [lem-sf-baer-criterion] therefore shows that $T=\Gamma_K(E)$ is injective as an $A$-module, as required.
